([[Sharpsburg, Georgia]]) | college = * [[Kennesaw State Owls men's basketball|Kennesaw State]] (2020–2023) * [[South Florida Bulls men's basketball|South Florida]] (2023–2024) * [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|full=y}} | team1 = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team2 = →[[Oklahoma City Blue]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team3 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team4 = →[[Rip City Remix]] | highlights = * [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|AAC co-Player of the Year]] (2024) * First-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2024) * First-team All-[[Atlantic Sun Conference|Atlantic Sun]] (2023) * Atlantic Sun All-Freshman team (2021) }} '''Christopher Youngblood''' (born February 9, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Rip City Remix]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kennesaw State Owls men's basketball|Kennesaw State Owls]], [[South Florida Bulls men's basketball|South Florida Bulls]], and [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. ==College career== Coming to Kennesaw State from [[East Coweta High School]], Youngblood was a three-year starter for the Owls. He averaged double-figures and improved his scoring average in each season. As a junior in the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 season]], he led the Owls to their first [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] berth, earning first-team All-[[Atlantic Sun Conference]] honors.{{cite news|first=Matthew|last=Morris|title= Chris Youngblood, Kennesaw State have ‘big-time opportunity’ |url= https://bvmsports.com/2023/03/08/chris-youngblood-kennesaw-state-have-big-time-opportunity/ | date = March 8, 2023 | website= bvmsports.com | publisher = BVM Sports|access-date=April 25, 2024}} After three seasons at Kennesaw State, Youngblood followed coach [[Amir Abdur-Rahim]], transferring to South Florida with Owl teammates Brandon Stroud and Kasen Jennings.{{cite news|first=Joey|last=Knight|title= 3 top Kennesaw State basketball players following their coach to USF |url= https://www.tampabay.com/sports/bulls/2023/04/04/usf-kennesaw-amir-abdur-rahim-chris-youngblood-brandon-stroud/ | date = April 4, 2023 | website= tampabay.com | publisher = [[Tampa Bay Times]]|access-date=April 25, 2024}} The trio led the Bulls to a surprising [[American Athletic Conference]] regular season title. Youngblood averaged 15.3 [[points per game]] and was named the [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|AAC co-Player of the Year]].{{cite news|title= Youngblood, Miguel Earn Top Awards as Three Bulls Land on AAC Postseason Teams |url= https://gousfbulls.com/news/2024/3/12/mens-basketball-youngblood-miguel-earn-top-awards-as-three-bulls-land-on-aac-postseason-teams.aspx | date = March 12, 2024 | website= gousfbulls.com | publisher = [[South Florida Bulls]]|access-date=April 25, 2024}} Following the 2023–24 season, Youngblood entered the transfer portal again.{{cite news|first=Joey|last=Knight|title= USF scoring leader Chris Youngblood entering NCAA transfer portal |url= https://www.mdjonline.com/usf-scoring-leader-chris-youngblood-entering-ncaa-transfer-portal/article_8e33d948-f75c-11ee-b3b1-dfb2ca765467.html | date = April 10, 2024 | website= mdjonline.com | publisher = [[Marietta Daily Journal]]|access-date=April 25, 2024}} He ultimately chose to play for coach [[Nate Oats]] at [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] in his hometown of [[Tuscaloosa, Alabama]].{{cite news|first=Nick|last=Alvarez|title= Alabama basketball adds Chris Youngblood, 2nd player from transfer portal |url= https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2024/04/alabama-basketball-adds-chris-youngblood-2nd-player-from-transfer-portal.html | date = April 13, 2024 | publisher = [[AL.com]]|access-date=April 25, bustingbrackets.com | publisher = [[FanSided]]|access-date=April 25, 2024}} ==Professional career== ===Oklahoma City Thunder / Blue (2025–26)=== After going undrafted in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Youngblood signed an [[NBA Summer League]] deal with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba-summer-league/boxscore/_/gameId/401793883/league/nba-summer-las-vegas|title=Thunder 90-81 Nets (Jul 10, 2025) Box Score|website=ESPN}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba-summer-league/boxscore/_/gameId/401793898/league/nba-summer-las-vegas|title=Thunder 104-85 Pacers (Jul 12, 2025) Box Score|website=ESPN}} After an impressive preseason with the team, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Thunder on October 18, 2025.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Chris Youngblood to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-youngblood-251018|date=October 18, 2025|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 18, 2025}} Youngblood made 32 appearances for Oklahoma City, recording averages of 2.0 points, 0.9 rebounds, and 0.3 assists. He was waived by the Thunder on February 6, 2026.{{Cite web |last=Martinez |first=Justin |title=OKC Thunder waives Chris Youngblood, signs Buddy Boeheim to two-way contract
